clue.text: Free to reject the Euro, keeping balance

indicators.note: to reject something is to throw it out, so a letter is dropped from the word for free

parts.note: to free someone is to liberate them
E is the abbreviation for the euro currency

explanation.surface: A country trying to get free of the single currency while keeping its economy balanced.
explanation.definitionFit: To librate is to oscillate or hold poised, a less common verb meaning to balance.

clue.text: Bizarre leavings of a hypnotist

indicators.note: bizarre means weird and distorted, so these letters are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: Strange leftovers found after a stage hypnotist has performed.
explanation.definitionFit: Svengali is the sinister mesmerist in du Maurier's novel Trilby, whose name now stands for any controlling hypnotist.

clue.text: Revolutionary got ear trouble

indicators.note: trouble here means something is upset or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebel leader came down with an earache.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Ortega led the Sandinista revolution in Nicaragua, an example of a revolutionary.

clue.text: Composer with anxiety over French place

parts.note: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned upward, so the word for anxiety is read backwards

parts.note: care means worry or anxiety

explanation.surface: A composer fretting about somewhere in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Bergerac is a town in the Dordogne region of south-west France.

clue.text: Ring audibly at St Clement's, say

definitions.meaning: a word sounding like wring, to twist, which this answer also means
St Clement Danes in London was built by Christopher Wren, so it is a ...., abbreviating church

explanation.surface: Ringing the bells out loud at a London church.
explanation.walkthrough: The bells of St Clement's feature in the nursery rhyme Oranges and Lemons, which steers you toward bell-ringing.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrench is to twist forcibly, the same as to wring; the second reading splits it as Wren plus Ch.

clue.text: Part of 13 for a dancer

definitions.meaning: 13 across begins with a word for puddings, and this meringue dessert is one
Anna ... was a celebrated Russian ballerina

explanation.surface: Someone from the shaving-lotion range is cast as a ballet performer.
explanation.walkthrough: The dessert was named after the ballerina, so both senses share one origin.
explanation.definitionFit: A pavlova is a meringue-and-fruit pudding; Pavlova was also a famous ballet dancer.

clue.text: Clerical journalist — vicar going round in a skirt

indicators.note: in means the reversed title is placed inside the garment

parts.note: a kilt is a Scottish pleated skirt

indicators.note: going round means turning about, so the abbreviation is written backwards

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a vicar's title

explanation.surface: A churchman who writes, picturing a clergyman spinning about in a kilt.
explanation.walkthrough: Francis Kilvert was a Victorian curate whose diary is a classic; journalist here means diarist, one who keeps a journal.
explanation.definitionFit: Kilvert was a Victorian clergyman famous for his diary, so a clerical journal-keeper.

clue.text: It's seen as great in a riot

definitions.text: It's seen as great in a riot

indicators.note: in a riot means wildly disordered, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Something that shows up in quantity when a crowd turns violent.
explanation.definitionFit: Police fire this irritant gas at rioters, so it is indeed seen during a riot.

clue.text: End of the road falls short of Keaton

parts.note: Buster Keaton was the silent film comedian
minus means lacking or falling short

explanation.surface: A film critic saying some work does not measure up to Keaton's.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus route's final stop is literally the end of the road for that bus.

clue.text: Order for fruit

definitions.meaning: the ... Order is a Protestant fraternal society in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A request placed for some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orange Order is a Protestant brotherhood; the citrus fruit shares the name.

clue.text: Rugby back goes easily with expedition

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: RU stands for Rugby Union
gently means easily, without force

explanation.surface: A rugby full-back jogs along comfortably on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: Back looks like a rugby position, but it reverses RU; expedition here means speed, not a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedition can mean promptness, so acting with expedition is acting with haste.

clue.text: It involves columns about tailless predator

indicators.note: tailless means the final letter is docked from the word

parts.note: a stoat is a small predatory mammal

explanation.surface: A news feature with columns about a predator missing its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa is a classical Greek covered walkway lined with a colonnade.

clue.text: Puddings have to go over the chin

parts.note: afters is British slang for dessert or pudding
taken as written

explanation.surface: Desserts must be eaten above a person's chin.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes what the lotion is for: it is put on to go over the shaved chin. AFTERS, British for dessert course, gives the first part.
explanation.definitionFit: A lotion splashed on after shaving is something applied to cover the chin and cheeks.

clue.text: One who does works of supererogation in Derbyshire?

definitions.text: One who does works of supererogation in Derbyshire?

parts.words: One who does works of supererogation in Derbyshire?
parts.note: read as a Boy Scout doing good deeds beyond duty, one even more kind than required; really a hill in the Peak District

explanation.surface: Describing an overachieving do-gooder living in the Peak District.
explanation.walkthrough: Kinder Scout is the highest point in the Peak District, Derbyshire; supererogation means doing more than duty requires.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase splits into a more kindly scout, but names the moorland plateau in Derbyshire.

clue.text: Refused 19, going the other way?

definitions.meaning: a hill sloping downward instead of up is a declining one

explanation.surface: Turned down a hard ascent by heading in the opposite direction.
explanation.definitionFit: To have declined is to have refused; a decline is also a slope going downward.

clue.text: Bangers going off scared the Yanks first

indicators.note: first means the abbreviation stands at the front of the answer

parts.note: US is short for the United States, home of the Yanks

indicators.note: going off means exploding, so these letters scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: Fireworks going off frightened the Americans first.
explanation.walkthrough: Bangers looks like fireworks or sausages, but is British slang for old cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Banger is British slang for an old, battered car, typically bought second-hand.

clue.text: A batsman is out

definitions.meaning: in cricket the batsman facing the bowling is the one on strike
a worker on strike is said to be out

explanation.surface: A cricketer has been dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: The batsman facing the bowler is the striker; a worker who has downed tools is a striker.

clue.text: Intellectually challenged class said to enjoy prior perception

indicators.note: said means the letters are those of what is spoken, not written

parts.note: 4C, a low-stream school form in a system ranking classes by ability from A down

explanation.surface: A slow-witted class supposedly gifted with second sight.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools forms were often streamed by ability, so 4C would be the weakest fourth-year class.
explanation.definitionFit: To foresee is to know in advance, that is, to have perception before an event.

clue.text: 1 in 4 perhaps

parts.note: read as a ratio or odds, but it is a road-sign gradient of one unit up for every four along

explanation.surface: A ratio that looks like odds or a statistic.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradient of one in four is very steep, a hard ascent for a road or path.

clue.text: Taking up drink gets a fellow high

indicators.note: in a down clue taking up means lifting, so the drink is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
Ted is any man's name

explanation.surface: A man takes to drink and gets intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling high means feeling exhilarated, the same as being elated.

clue.text: They initially evacuate into pots

indicators.note: into means the initial letter is placed inside the word for pots

parts.note: bowls are pots or basins

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter only

explanation.surface: Something that empties into chamber pots.
explanation.definitionFit: The intestines are what empty, usually into a toilet bowl or pot.

clue.text: Old tribe in reflective manner

indicators.note: reflective suggests a mirror image, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: mode means a way or manner

explanation.surface: An ancient people who behaved thoughtfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Edom was an ancient kingdom of the Edomites, descendants of Esau in the Bible.

clue.text: Part of 13 to shove one into ill-fitting suit

indicators.note: into means the other letters are pushed inside the rearranged suit
ill-fitting suggests something out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: ram means to push forcefully
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Part of a grooming product used to force someone into a badly cut suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 across starts with a British word for desserts, and this Italian pudding is one.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is an Italian coffee-flavoured dessert, one example of a pudding.

clue.text: Jam makers shuffling deck, which is very wrong

parts.note: the WI, Women's Institute, is a British women's group famous for making jam

indicators.note: shuffling means mixing cards, so the word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ladies from a jam-making group stacking a card deck, which is cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Institute is a British countryside organisation stereotyped for jam and cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wicked is evil or grossly immoral, very wrong indeed.

clue.text: Father loses name, but remains highly esteemed

indicators.note: loses means a letter is dropped from the title

parts.note: a priest, Father, is addressed as Reverend

explanation.surface: A priest who loses his reputation yet is still respected.
explanation.definitionFit: Revered means deeply respected, held in high esteem.

clue.text: Frightened by hood with a gun

parts.note: Al Capone was a notorious hood, or gangster
armed means carrying a weapon

explanation.surface: Scared by a gangster carrying a firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: Hood is American slang for hoodlum, here Al Capone.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alarmed means being frightened or suddenly anxious.
